title: 12 Underrated South Carolina Towns You Can Still Retire on Social Security Alone
fullText: South Carolina's real estate industry does not want you to see this video because the 12 towns I'm about to show you make every overpriced Charleston condo look like a financial mistake and they make every Hilton Head golf community look like a trap disguised as a retirement dream. I have been doing the research on this one for a long time and what I found surprised even me. We are talking about real towns, not dying ghost towns, not floodprone coastal gambles, but actual livable charming South Carolina communities where your social security check does the job all by itself. Where a median home costs under $130,000, where a one-bedroom apartment can be had for under $800 a month, and where the average retired worker's monthly benefit of around $2,76 in 2026 does not just stretch. It actually breathes. Before we get into the countdown, I want to be upfront about something most of these videos skip. South Carolina is not a no income tax state. It has a state income tax. But here is what they forget to mention. South Carolina fully exempts social security income from state taxes. On top of that, retirees get a generous deduction on other retirement income, which for a social security-only retiree means your effective state tax burden is close to zero. That matters. Now, let's get into the list. Number 12, Gaffne. You roll into Gaffne on Interstate 85 and you see it before you see anything else. A million gallon water tower painted to look exactly like a giant peach complete with the crease. It is simultaneously the most ridiculous and most endearing thing you will ever see from a highway. Welcome to Cherokee County. Gaffne sits in the upstate about 55 mi southwest of Charlotte, North Carolina. The population hovers around 12,000 and the town has held on to that size without the growing pains that have inflated prices in nearby Spartanberg and Greenville. The numbers here are genuinely striking. The median home price in Gaffne is around $95,000 as of mid 2026. A one-bedroom apartment rents for roughly $600 to $750 a month. The overall cost of living in Gaffne runs approximately 23% below the national average. The nearest full service hospital is Cherokee Medical Center right in town about 2 miles from Main Street. That water tower, officially called the Peachoid, was built in 1981 and became nationally famous when House of Cards used Gaffne as a filming location and featured it prominently. It has been photographed by every major news outlet in America. Locals have mixed feelings about that particular legacy, but they will tell you about it within 20 minutes of meeting you. On $2,76 a month, you are looking at mortgage payments on a modest home under $600 here, leaving well over $1,400 for everything else. Groceries, utilities, prescription co-pays, all of which cost less in Gaffne than the national benchmark suggests. The honest caveat, Gaffne is inland and has essentially zero hurricane risk, which is a genuine advantage. But the job market is thin if you need supplemental income and specialist medical care beyond what Cherokee Medical offers means a 30inut drive to Spartanberg. The town carries higher than average violent crime for its size. So neighborhood selection matters more here than in some other towns on this list. Number 11, Union. Union County is one of those places South Carolina guide books tend to skip entirely [music] and that oversight is exactly why it is on this list. Union is the county seat of Union County, tucked between Spartanberg and Chester in the upstate about 60 mi southwest of Charlotte. The population is around 7,000 in the city proper with the surrounding county adding another 20,000 people. The numbers in Union are among the lowest in the entire state. Median home prices sit around $75 to $85,000. Rent for a one-bedroom can be found for $550 to $700 a month. The overall cost of living runs roughly 25 to 28% below the national average. Wallace Thompson Hospital serves the area located about one mile from the town center. Here is the wildcard fact that nobody leads with. Union County has an abandoned Monarch Mill complex dating back to 1902. A massive Gothic looking textile fortress whose brick facads and smoke stack define the town's visual identity in a way that is hard to fully describe until you stand in front of it. Local preservationists have been working to restore it for years, and that tension between industrial heritage and forward momentum is woven into everything about how this town sees itself. For social security retirees who need to stretch every dollar, Union is hard to beat. A modest home here can be purchased outright for under $85,000, leaving nearly all of a monthly Social Security benefit free for living expenses. That math simply does not work in most of America anymore. The caveat, Union has faced economic headwinds for decades, and while the town is stable, amenities are limited. The nearest regional medical complex with full specialist services is Spartanberg Medical Center, about 35 mi away. Crime statistics run higher than most smaller upstate towns, so do your research on specific streets and neighborhoods before you commit. Number 10, Marian. Marian is a small city of about 6,000 people in Marian County, tucked in the PD region of northeastern South Carolina, about 30 miles inland from Myrtle Beach. And that geographic position, close enough to the coast for a day trip, far enough to completely skip the tourist pricing, is a genuine advantage that most retirees overlook entirely. Median home prices in Marian run around $75 to $90,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically falls between $550 and $700 a month. Cost of living runs about 25% below the national average. Mloud Health Marian is in town. A regional hospital facility operated by one of South Carolina's major health networks. The wild card. Marian County was the home territory of Francis Marion, the Revolutionary War guerilla commander known as the Swamp Fox. His hitandrun tactics against British forces in the Carolina back country were so effective that military strategists now point to them as the foundational model for what we call asymmetric warfare. The county is deeply proud of this heritage and the local museum, historic markers, and the university bearing his name reflect it at every turn. For a retiree on social security, Marian offers some of the most affordable housing on this entire list. Under $90,000 for a medianpriced home, under 700 a month to rent a one-bedroom. And if you time your Myrtle Beach visits to the shoulder season, spring and fall, you enjoy world-class beaches 45 minutes away without paying coastal prices to actually live there. The caveat, Marian County carries significant rural poverty, and the job market is extremely limited for anyone considering part-time supplemental income. For specialist care beyond what Mloud Health Marian provides, the drive to Florence or Myrtle Beach is 30 to 45 minutes. Cell coverage in parts of the rural county can be spotty. Number nine, Clinton. Clinton is a small college town in the southern end of Lawren County about 50 mi southeast of Greenville and 45 mi from Greenwood. The population is around 9,000. Presbyterian College, a small liberal arts school with genuine division 2 athletics, and a real campus feel gives the town an intellectual pulse you would not necessarily predict at this price point. Median home prices in Clinton average around $15 to $115,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically runs between $620 and $775 monthly. Cost of living comes in around 20 to 22% below the national average. The nearest hospital is Lawrence County Memorial Hospital, about 12 miles away in the neighboring city of Lawrence. Here is the wild card. Clinton is home to the Witten Center, one of the oldest facilities in the country dedicated [music] to serving people with intellectual disabilities. Founded in 1893, it has been a major employer in this area for over 130 years. Locals will tell you it shaped Clinton's unusual blend of community pride and quiet, steady resilience. For a retiree, the Presbyterian College campus adds walking trails, a library, cultural events, and sports programming open to community members at low or no cost. This is a meaningful quality of life boost that does not show up in any cost of living index. A two-bedroom home in Clinton can be purchased for under $130,000. And for a renter paying $700 a month, that leaves over $1,300 free each month for everything else. The caveat, the 12mm drive to the nearest hospital is worth noting for anyone managing ongoing health conditions. Clinton's downtown retail scene is modest, and major grocery shopping and most big box retail require a drive of 20 to 30 minutes. Number eight, Laurens. Lawren is a quiet courthouse town of about 10,000 people in Lawren County, about 35 mi southeast of Greenville. Wide streets, canopied oaks, and a courthouse square that was built for a slower pace of life. One that, if you are retiring, might feel like exactly what you have been looking for. The median home price in Laurens runs around $110,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically comes in between $600 and $775 a month. Cost of living is about 20% below the national average. Lawrence County Memorial Hospital is right in town. Here is the strange but true hook. When the textile mills that employed most of Lawrence closed in the 1990s and early 2000s, the town entered a prolonged, painful economic decline. The unintended silver lining is that the decline kept prices suppressed and they have stayed low even as the town has quietly stabilized around healthcare, education, and light manufacturing. You are essentially benefiting from a long economic correction that kept values realistic while other parts of the state overheated. For a retiree, Lawren delivers a walkable courthouse square, a YMCA, and proximity to Lake Greenwood for fishing and boating, all without the price tags of towns closer to Greenville. $2,076 a month goes a very long way here. The honest caveat, Lawrence County Memorial Hospital is a smaller regional facility. If you have complex chronic conditions requiring frequent specialist visits, you will be driving to Greenville regularly. The interstate is not adjacent, so the rural solitude comes with real logistical trade-offs. Number seven, Abbeville. Abbeville calls itself the birthplace and the death place of the Confederacy. And while that history is complicated and charged, the town's physical legacy of Antabbellum architecture, one of the most stunning courthouse squares in South Carolina and a fully restored 1908 opera house, creates something genuinely extraordinary for a community of 5,000 people. Abbyville sits in the western corner of the state in Abavville County, about 30 mi southwest of Greenwood and 45 miles from Anderson. It is deep upstate, which means lower humidity than the coast, essentially zero hurricane risk, and a fourseason climate that many retirees from the Midwest or Mid-Atlantic find familiar and comfortable. The median home price in Abyville runs around $100,000 to $115,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically falls between $575 and $750 monthly. Cost of living is approximately 22% below the national average. Self-regional health care in Greenwood, about 28 miles away, is the primary regional hospital for this area. The wild card. On May 2nd, 1865, in the Bert Stark mansion right on Abbeville's historic square, Jefferson Davis held the last official Confederate cabinet meeting of the Civil War. Within days, the Confederacy effectively ceased to exist as a functioning government. The mansion still stands, still gives guided tours, and still marks that specific, irreversible moment in American history in a way that you can feel when you walk through the door. For a retiree, Abbeville's Opera House offers live professional theater productions year round at prices a retiree budget can actually absorb. The historic district is genuinely walkable. The surrounding Lake Country with Lake Thurman and Lake Russell both nearby provides fishing, boating, and outdoor recreation access at a level that would cost far more anywhere else in the southeast. The honest caveat, specialist medical care requiring a full hospital stay means a drive of more than 30 minutes to Greenwood. The town is beautiful but isolated. If driving becomes difficult later in retirement, that isolation becomes a real logistical challenge that no amount of charm can fix. Number six, Orangeberg. Orangeberg sits at the crossroads of Interstate [music] 26 and Highway 301, about 40 mi southeast of Columbia and 80 mi northwest of Charleston. Population around 13,000 in the city. It is home to two historically black universities, South Carolina State University and Claflin University, which give it a cultural depth and intellectual energy that genuinely catches firsttime visitors offguard. The numbers are compelling. Median home prices in Orangeburg run around 95 to $110,000. Rent for a one-bedroom comes in between $625 and $800 a month. Cost of living is approximately 22% below the national average. The Regional Medical Center of Orangeberg and Calhoun counties is right in town, a fullervice regional hospital with over 300 beds. The wild card. In February of 1968, state highway patrol officers opened fire on student demonstrators at South Carolina State University, killing three young men and wounding 27 others. The Orangeberg Massacre remains one of the most consequential and least discussed civil rights tragedies in American history. The town carries that weight with a particular dignified seriousness, and the campus reflects it in ways that make you stop and think. For a retiree, Orangeberg offers something rare on this list. A fullervice regional hospital right in town. No long drive for an emergency. The university presence brings lectures, concerts, athletic events, and cultural programming year round, and housing prices have stayed affordable even as the Interstate 26 corridor has grown steadily around it. The caveat, Orangeberg sits in the inner coastal plane, and while it is not on the coast, the region can see significant inland flooding during major hurricane events. Flood risk is lower than coastal communities, but it is not zero. Run the FEMA flood zone maps on any specific property before you buy. Before we continue, if you have not subscribed to Carolina Living yet, this is the channel that brings you the real numbers on South Carolina, not the glossy brochure version. Hit subscribe so you do not miss the rest of this list. Number five, Batesburg Leville. This town has a hyphenated name because it is technically two communities that grew together along the Lexington Saluda County line and never fully merged into a single identity. Locals just call it Batesburg or Leville depending entirely on which side of town they grew up on. Batesburg Leville sits about 30 mi west of Colombia, close enough to the state capital for real amenities far enough to keep housing prices in a completely different universe. The population is around 6,000. The surrounding Saluda County area has been called one of the last truly affordable pockets within realistic driving distance of a major South Carolina city. Median home prices here run around $115 to $130,000. One-bedroom rents typically come in between $650 and $800 a month. Cost of living runs approximately 18 to 20% below the national average. The nearest major hospital is Lexington Medical Center in West Colombia, about 30 mi east, a large, well-resourced regional system with full specialty coverage. The wildcard Batesburg Leville was once celebrated as the onion capital of South Carolina. In the early 20th century, it shipped more onions per capita than any other town in the state. There are descendants of those farming families who will tell you this with complete sincerity and genuine pride. And the agricultural identity still shapes how this community sees itself in a way that feels nothing like the brochure version of smalltown southern identity. For retirees, proximity to Columbia means access to the University of South Carolina's Koger Center for the Arts, Riverbank Zoo, major shopping, full medical specialty systems, and a major airport, all within a halfhour drive. But you are paying Batesburg Leville housing prices, not Colombia prices. That gap is real and powerful and it is not going to stay this wide much longer. The caveat [music] that 30-m drive to Lexington Medical is manageable for most non-emergency situations, but for a midnight cardiac event, it matters. This lifestyle works best for active, independently mobile retirees who are not yet dependent on frequent specialist visits close to home. Number four, Walterboro. [music] Walterboro brands itself the front porch of the Low Country, and that description is more accurate than most tourism taglines deserve. It sits at the edge where inland upstate culture meets the tidal flats and Spanish moss draped live oaks of the Low Country, capturing something from both worlds without fully belonging to either, which turns out to be a genuinely appealing quality in a place to live. Walterboroough is the seat of Colatin County about 50 miles west of Charleston and about 30 miles north of the coast. Population around 5,000 in the city. The surrounding landscape is extraordinary. And the ACE Basin, one of the largest undeveloped estuarian ecosystems on the east coast, sits right there and draws burers, kayakers, and nature photographers from across the country every year. Median home prices in Walterboro run around $115 to $130,000. Rent for a one-bedroom falls between $650 and $825 monthly. Cost of living runs approximately 18% below the national average. Colatin Medical Center is in town, a fullervice hospital about a mile from the historic district. The wild card, Walterboroough, gained entirely unexpected national attention in early 2023 as the venue for the Alex Murdo double murder trial, a courtroom drama that drew wall-to-wall media coverage for weeks and turned this quiet lowcountry courthouse town into one of the most Googled locations in America. The locals had profoundly mixed feelings about the spotlight. The courthouse is now a minor stop on the true crime tourism circuit, which is as strange a legacy as any small American town has ever inherited. For a retiree, Walterboro offers a real small town downtown with antique shops, locallyowned restaurants, and a wildlife sanctuary located within the actual city limits. The Ace Basin Access adds a recreational dimension that many coastal communities charge a steep premium to be near. And having a full-ervice hospital in town at this price point is a meaningful practical advantage. The honest caveat, Walter Burough sits in Colatin County, a low country county with genuine flood risk during major tropical events. It is not on the coast, but storm surge and inland flooding from significant hurricanes can reach this area through river systems. Flood zone maps must be part of your due diligence before buying here. And for complex specialist care, the drive to Charleston is 50 miles. If you are getting value from this breakdown, tap the like button before we get to the top three. It genuinely helps this information reach the people who need it most. Number three, Lancaster. Lancaster sits in Lancaster County in the northern Piedmont of South Carolina, about 40 miles south of Charlotte, North Carolina. The population is around 10,000 in the city with the county pushing toward 100,000. And that proximity to Charlotte without paying Charlotte prices is the defining advantage that puts Lancaster in the top three. Median home prices in Lancaster City run around $120 to $140,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically falls between $700 and $850 monthly. Cost of living is approximately 16 to 18% below the national average. Springs Memorial Hospital is in town, a full-ervice regional hospital with emergency cardiac, surgical, and specialty services right there in Lancaster. The wild card. Lancaster is the documented birthplace of Andrew Jackson, the seventh president of the United States. There is a state historic site, a dedicated museum, and an annual festival that the community takes more seriously than most heritage events in South Carolina. Locals will tell you about it within 20 minutes of meeting you, whether or not you asked. For a retiree, Lancaster offers something this list rarely gets to deliver. A fullervice hospital in town, a functioning retail ecosystem with major grocery chains and a real downtown, and access to the Charlotte metro's worldclass medical systems just 40 m north. Atrium Health and Novant Health, two of the largest regional hospital networks in the Southeast, are within a manageable drive for specialist appointments. Social Security Math in Lancaster. A retiree with a $600 monthly mortgage on a modest home clears $1,476 for living expenses in a county where daily costs run 16 to 18% below the national average. That math works tightly, but it works. And that is more than most Americans can say about any retirement option within an hour of a major metro. The honest caveat, Lancaster County has seen some of the fastest home price appreciation in South Carolina over the last 3 years, driven by Charlotte's southward suburban expansion. Prices are rising and they are not slowing down. If you are considering Lancaster, the window is open, but move with urgency because this entry will look meaningfully different by 2028. Number two, York. York is the county seat of York County in the northern Piedmont of South Carolina. about 30 mi south of Charlotte and 15 mi from Rock Hill. The population is around 8,000 in the city itself. And while York County overall has become expensive in places like Fort Mill and Tega K due to Charlotte's growth, the city of York, the actual historic courthouse town, has remained surprisingly and stubbornly affordable. Median home prices in the city of York run around $130 to $150,000. Rent for a one-bedroom falls between 750 and $925 monthly. Cost of living in York County runs about 12 to 15% below the national average. Piedmont Medical Center in Rock Hill about 15 miles away is a fullervice regional hospital with cardiac surgery, oncology, and emergency services. The wild card. York's historic district is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and the town contains a concentration of antibbellum homes that survived the Civil War almost entirely intact, partially because William Tecumpsa Sherman's destructive march through South Carolina cut through other parts of the state and largely bypassed this corner of the Piedmont. The architecture here is authentic in a way that reproduction resort communities charge 200,000 extra to recreate from scratch. For a retiree at number two on this list, York delivers a genuinely walkable historic downtown with locallyowned restaurants, independent shops, and a small but real arts and cultural scene. A hospital system 15 miles away that can handle complex care and proximity to the full Charlotte Metro, major airports, worldclass medical facilities, professional sports, live music, and international dining without paying Charlotte prices to access any of it. On $2,76 a month in York, you are looking at housing costs in the $800 to $900 range, leaving over $1,100 for living expenses in a county that runs below the national cost average. That math works. It works in a place with genuine charm, genuine history, and genuine proximity to serious resources when you need them. The honest caveat, York County overall has been appreciating steadily and prices within York City have moved upward compared to 2 and 3 years ago. The Charlotte shadow is long and keeps creeping south. York City has held its affordability better than Fort Mill or Tega, but that is not going to last forever. Buy or rent here with the understanding that this window is finite. And number [music] one, the town that hits every metric simultaneously. Affordable housing, a hospital in town, cultural life, inland storm safety, a college presence, and a quality of life that outperforms its price tag by a margin that frankly embarrasses places charging three times as much. Number one is Newberry. Newberry sits in Newberry County in the geographic middle of the state, about 40 miles northwest of Columbia and an hour from Greenville. population around 11,000. Newberry College, a private liberal arts school with a real athletics program, gives the town a heartbeat that most communities this size simply do not have. And then there is the opera house. Not a converted warehouse, not a community theater in a strip mall, [music] an actual operating 1882 opera house right on Main Street, producing live professional theater, concerts, and cultural events every single season. It is a building that would be the crown jewel of a city four times this size. And it is sitting here in a town where you can buy a three-bedroom house for under $130,000. Median home prices in Newberry sit around $15,000. Rent for a one-bedroom typically falls between $650 and $800 monthly. The overall cost of living runs more than 21% below the national average. Newberry County Memorial Hospital is in town. A critical access hospital about a mile from Main Street, Columbia's Prisma Health System with full specialty and surgical coverage is 40 miles southeast. Here is the wildcard fact that earns the number one slot. Newberry Colleg's football team regularly competes in the NCAA Division 2 National Playoffs. Fall Saturdays in this small town generate genuine college game day energy with a packed stadium. Woom, main street alive, tailgates, the whole thing. Most retirees relocating from bigger cities absolutely do not see that coming. It is an unexpectedly joyful feature of daily life here that no data set captures. Lake Murray is 20 m southeast offering boating, fishing, and lakefront recreation within a halfhour drive. Greenville is an hour northwest with worldclass dining, a nationally recognized downtown, a major airport, and one of the South's best medical systems. Colombia is 40 mi east with the state capital, USC, Riverbanks, Zoo, the Koger Center, and every specialty hospital service you could need. Newberry sits in the center of all of it, paying none of those city's housing costs. On $2,76 a month, Newberry delivers. A retiree who buys a modest home at $15,000 with a reasonable down payment C might carry a mortgage under $550 a month, leaving over $1,500 for living expenses in one of the most affordable cost environments in the entire Southeast. A renter paying $750 a month still clears over $1,300 for everything else. That is real money, real freedom, real retirement. The honest caveat because this channel does not skip the truth. Newberry County Memorial Hospital is a smaller critical access facility. For cardiac surgery, cancer treatment, or major surgery, you are going 40 miles to Colombia. That drive matters and you should plan for it. But for the day-to-day rhythm of healthy retirement, routine checkups, urgent care, preventive screenings, and physical therapy, Newberry handles it in town. Here is what I want you to take away from this entire list. The real estate industry, the resort developers, the branded retirement communities with the guarded gates and the glossy brochures. They need you to believe that retiring well in South Carolina requires a coastal address or a golf cart community with a homeowners association telling you what color to paint your shutters. 12 towns just proved otherwise. Real affordability, real hospitals, real culture, and real lives. All within reach of a social security check that the national headlines keep telling you is barely enough to survive on. It is enough. In the right zip code, it is more than enough. And now you know 12 of those zip codes. Tell me in the comments which of these 12 towns surprised you most. And if you have already made the move to one of these places, or if you are still doing your research, tell us where you are in the planning process. Drop your age in the comments, too. I want to know who is watching this and what stage of retirement planning you are in. That realworld information is worth more than any data set I can pull. And it might be exactly what someone else watching right now needs to hear to finally make the move.
fullTextVi: Ngành bất động sản Nam Carolina không muốn bạn xem video này vì 12 thị trấn mà tôi sắp cho bạn xem khiến mọi căn hộ đắt đỏ ở Charleston trông thật giống như một sai lầm tài chính và chúng khiến mọi cộng đồng chơi gôn của Hilton Head trông giống như một cái bẫy được ngụy trang dưới dạng giấc mơ nghỉ hưu. Tôi đã nghiên cứu về vấn đề này trong một thời gian dài và những gì tôi tìm thấy làm tôi ngạc nhiên. Chúng ta đang nói về những thị trấn thực sự, không phải những thị trấn ma sắp chết, không phải những canh bạc ven biển ngập lụt, nhưng các cộng đồng Nam Carolina quyến rũ thực sự có thể sống được, nơi kiểm tra an sinh xã hội của bạn thực hiện công việc của chính nó. Nơi một ngôi nhà trung bình có giá dưới 130.000 USD, nơi có thể có căn hộ một phòng ngủ với mức lương dưới 800 USD một tháng và mức trợ cấp hàng tháng trung bình của người lao động đã nghỉ hưu là khoảng 2,76 USD vào năm 2026 không chỉ kéo dài. Nó thực sự thở. Trước khi chúng ta bắt đầu đếm ngược, tôi muốn nói thẳng về điều gì đó nhất bỏ qua những video này. Nam Carolina không phải là tiểu bang không có thuế thu nhập. Nó có thuế thu nhập của tiểu bang. Nhưng đây là những gì họ quên đề cập đến. Nam Carolina miễn hoàn toàn thu nhập an sinh xã hội từ thuế tiểu bang. Ngoài ra, những người về hưu còn được khấu trừ một khoản lớn vào thu nhập hưu trí khác, đối với người nghỉ hưu chỉ nhận an sinh xã hội có nghĩa là gánh nặng thuế tiểu bang thực tế của bạn gần với zero. Điều đó quan trọng. Bây giờ chúng ta hãy vào danh sách. Số 12, Gaffne. Bạn rẽ vào Gaffne trên Xa lộ Liên tiểu bang 85 và bạn nhìn thấy nó trước khi nhìn thấy bất cứ điều gì khác. Tháp nước triệu gallon được sơn giống hệt quả đào khổng lồ hoàn chỉnh với nếp gấp. Đó đồng thời là điều nực cười nhất và đáng yêu nhất mà bạn từng thấy từ một đường cao tốc. Chào mừng đến với Quận Cherokee. Gaffne nằm ở ngoại ô cách Charlotte, Bắc Carolina khoảng 55 dặm về phía tây nam. Dân số dao động khoảng 12.000 người và thị trấn vẫn giữ được quy mô đó mà không gặp phải những khó khăn ngày càng tăng khiến giá cả tăng cao ở Spartanberg và Greenville gần đó. Những con số ở đây thực sự ấn tượng. Giá nhà trung bình ở Gaffne là khoảng 95.000 USD tính đến giữa năm 2026. Căn hộ một phòng ngủ có giá thuê khoảng 600 đến 750 USD một tháng. Tổng chi phí sinh hoạt ở Gaffne thấp hơn mức trung bình toàn quốc khoảng 23%. Bệnh viện đầy đủ dịch vụ gần nhất là Trung tâm Y tế Cherokee ngay trong thị trấn khoảng 2 dặm từ Main Street. Tháp nước đó, có tên chính thức là Peachoid, được xây dựng vào năm 1981 và được cấp quốc gia nổi tiếng khi House of Cards sử dụng Gaffne làm địa điểm quay phim và giới thiệu nó nổi bật.
